name: Barpak Ghale
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Yoshida, Shigeki. 2024. A phonological sketch of Barpak Ghale. Tokyo University Linguistic Papers (TULIP) 46: 359-393. DOI 10.15083/0002010733 (open access, UTokyo repository). Corroborated by Khadgi, Mari-Sisko. 2021. Segmental and tonal phonology of Barpak Ghale. Helsinki: University of Helsinki dissertation, 304 pp., hdl:10138/336481.
catalog_locator: p. 359 (Abstract); p. 378 (§5.1 Tone on free morphemes); p. 381 (§5.3 Tone realization in words, opening sentence); p. 382 (§5.3, 'The pitch of a bound morpheme matches that of the end of the preceding syllable'). Khadgi 2021 (printed pages): p. 74 §4.2, p. 63 §3.4.1, p. 92, p. 150.
catalog_quote: The description includes the phoneme inventory, tone, syllable structures, consonant clusters, and both segmental and suprasegmental morphophonological processes, but not stress and intonation. [p. 359] ... Each lexical morpheme has its own tone. The realization of tone is different for monosyllabic morphemes and polysyllabic morphemes. [p. 378] ... The /55/ tone is realized on disyllabic words with the first syllable pronounced higher, using the same pitch as a monosyllabic word with /55/, and the second syllable pronounced lower. In disyllabic words with the low falling tone /21/, the pitch gradually lowers from the first syllable to the second syllable. In disyllabic words with the rising tone /25/, both the first and second syllables have level pitch with the first pronounced low and the second pronounced high. [p. 378] ... As in other Tamangish languages (Mazaudon 2005), Barpak Ghale has a word-tone system where the prosodic pattern of a word, formed from a root and bound morphemes, is determined by the root tone. [p. 381] ... The pitch of a bound morpheme matches that of the end of the preceding syllable. [p. 382]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened: (35 pp., printed pages 359-393; p.1 = p.359). All three quoted fragments are present verbatim at the stated locators: (1) p. 359 Abstract: "The description includes the phoneme inventory, tone, syllable structures, consonant clusters, and both segmental and suprasegmental morphophonological processes, but not stress and intonation."; (2) p. 378 §5.1 Tone on free morphemes, first sentence: "Each lexical morpheme has its own tone."; (3) p. 381 §5.3 Tone realization in words, first sentence: "As in other Tamangish languages (Mazaudon 2005), Barpak Ghale has a word-tone system where the prosodic pattern of a word, formed from a root and bound morphemes, is determined by the root to…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Barpak (Southern) Ghale is a word-tone language with five contrastive tones (/55/, /33/, /22/, /21/, /25/) borne by the morpheme and spread over the whole word; the root's tone fixes the pitch pattern of the word including atonal suffixes/clitics. No source states where word stress falls; the most detailed phonology (Yoshida 2024) explicitly leaves stress and intonation undescribed, and the 304-page dissertation (Khadgi 2021) never locates stress either.
new_statements.exceptions: Tonal suffixes (e.g. -pi55, =ju55) carry their own tone; the past suffix -te and ergative =te pattern with clitics; stem tone alternations before certain suffixes (Yoshida 2024 §6.2; Yoshida 2026). Khadgi 2021: 196 notes Nishi reported only four tones for Keura Ghale.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone domain = morpheme in the lexicon, word in the sentence (Khadgi 2021: 74; Yoshida 2024: 381). Yoshida 2024 §5.1 describes pitch realisations of tones on di- and trisyllabic words (e.g. /55/ high on first syllable, lower on second) — these are tone realisations, not stress. Khadgi 2021 §4.5: no question intonation; focus/emotion prosody briefly discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All first-hand phonological sources (Khadgi 2021; Yoshida 2024a,b; 2026; Paudel 2008) describe the Barpak village dialect (Glottolog barp1238) of Southern Ghale [sout2715, ISO ghe]; Nishi 1982/1983 analysed the Keura/Kyaura dialect (kyau1238). Ethnologue's Northern (ghh) vs Southern (ghe) split is called inconclusive by Khadgi 2021: 5. Paudel 2008 (the sole Glottolog descriptive reference) is a grammar sketch whose phonology section, per Khadgi, was copied from her unpublished ms.

tone_statements.citation: 西 義郎 [Nishi, Yoshio]. 1982. ネパールの－チベット・ビルマ語系言語－ガレ語の調査について [On the survey of Ghale, a Tibeto-Burman language of Nepal]. 南海研紀要 (Memoirs of the Kagoshima University Research Center for the South Pacific) 3(1): 139-167. Kagoshima: Kagoshima University.
tone_statements.quote: (シーワード氏の資料は不統一なので，私の採録したガレ語ケウラ方言形（Keura）でガレ語形を代表して示す。なお，この方言では，破裂音と破擦音の系例に無声音対有声音の対立がない。声調は次の４種である：高平/´/，中平（無表記），中/低昇/ˇ/，中/低降/`/ ...) ... [注6] 一応音韻化してあるが，声調（とくに２音節以上の語について）は更に検討を要する。... Keura方言には，２２ケの子音音素と６ケの母音音素が立てられる。... 声調は，上記の４ケである。
tone_statements.translation: (Since Mr Seaward's material is inconsistent, I represent the Ghale forms by the Keura dialect forms of Ghale that I recorded myself. In this dialect there is no voiceless vs voiced opposition in the stop and affricate series. The tones are the following four: high level /´/, mid level (unmarked), mid/low rising /ˇ/, mid/low falling /`/ ...) ... [fn.6] The forms are provisionally phonemicised, but the tones (especially of words of two or more syllables) need further examination. ... For the Keura dialect 22 consonant phonemes and 6 vowel phonemes are set up. ... The tones are the four given above.
tone_statements.locator: p.145, end of section 1; footnote 6 on p.148
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Four tones (high level, mid level, mid/low rising, mid/low falling) in Keura dialect, author's fieldwork; polysyllable tones provisional; Ghale and Tamang tones don't correspond (fn.7). No stress.

sources.note: Abstract p. 359: the description covers phonemes, tone, syllable structure, clusters and morphophonology 'but not stress and intonation'. Section 5 (pp. 377-383): five word tones /55 33 22 21 25/, each lexical morpheme has its own tone, word-tone system in which the root tone determines the pitch pattern of root + bound morphemes; pitch realizations on di-/trisyllables described (e.g. /55/ = high first syllable, lower second). No statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Khadgi, Mari-Sisko. 2021. Segmental and tonal phonology of Barpak Ghale: Typological, methodological and theoretical perspectives. Helsinki: University of Helsinki dissertation. 304 pp. hdl:10138/336481.
sources.note: Full segmental + tonal phonology with acoustic and perceptual studies. Ch. 4: tone is phonemic, five contrastive tones (p. 70); 'the tone-bearing unit is the morpheme. Each morpheme has its own tone, apart from some suffixes' (p. 74); 4.5 Intonation and tone (pp. 84-88): no question intonation, focus etc. The word 'stress' occurs only in generic remarks (p. 63 vowel variation 'whether the syllable is stressed or not'; general prosody theory pp. 92, 152). No statement locating word stress in Ghale.
